advances: A second-order necessary condition for the actual normal of a smoothed fixed-body fixed-source cap, including positive-area supporting strip endpoints.
author: PK-research-agent
proof:
Expand the smooth positive normalizer using $\Gamma(u)=1$: its first and second derivatives are $\gamma$ and $\eta$. The first two derivatives of $m_t=(N+tD)\cdot(w-Y)/\Gamma(u+tv)$ are consequently the stated $k$ and $-2\gamma k-\eta m$, uniformly on the compact fiber union. The normal integral is differentiable at zero for a smooth kernel and for the ramp. In the latter case the kink planes have zero $d$-volume in each fiber and the difference quotients are bounded. Stationarity gives $\int\psi(q)k\,d\mu/h=0$. Also $\int m\psi(q)\,d\mu/h=A-bS$. Twice differentiating a $C^2$ CDF on the compact argument range gives the smooth formula. Polarization yields the bilinear form. The direction $D=N$ has $k=\eta=0$, and a pure-base direction has $\gamma=\eta=0$.

For the ramp, use the difference of the two integrated hinges $[m_t+b+h]_+$ and $[m_t+b]_+$, divided by $h$. For either hinge denote its old affine argument by $\ell$ and its first and second margin derivatives by $k,j$. The difference of the hinge values at $\ell+t k+t^2j/2+o(t^2)$ and at $\ell+tk$, divided by $t^2/2$, tends almost everywhere to $j\mathbf1_{\ell>0}$. It is bounded uniformly by the Lipschitz property of the hinge and the uniform expansion, so the same holds after integration. For the remaining linear perturbation, subtract $\ell_++t k\mathbf1_{\ell>0}$. In continuous normal coordinates $\xi$ tangent to the old plane and $s=\ell/\|u\|$, the residual lies in $|s|\le C|t|$ and is bounded by $C|t|$. At fixed $\xi$, after substituting $s=t r/\|u\|$ for $t>0$, the scaled residual has the one-dimensional hinge triangle with increment $k(\xi,0)$, since $k(\xi,s)\to k(\xi,0)$ uniformly there. A triangle of area $k^2/2$ lies on the negative old side if $k>0$, and on the positive old side if $k<0$. Almost every line through a proper section crosses both sides of the plane. A line through a relative-interior point of a positive-area supporting facet extends to the body side: interpolate a nearby point of the facet with a fixed interior point, adjusting the tangential coordinate to the chosen line. Lines missing the section have zero limit by compactness, and section relative boundaries or lower-dimensional contacts are null. The residual strip bound gives domination in the tangential integral. Thus the right second coefficient (with factor $2/t^2$) is full $k^2$ on proper sections, $[k]_-^2$ on positive-side supporting sections, and $[k]_+^2$ on negative-side supporting sections, with coarea divisor $\|u\|$. In $d=1$ this is interval integration and counting coarea.

Subtract the two hinge expansions. Their smooth second terms differ by $\int j\psi(q)\,d\mu/h$, which is $(bS-A)\eta$ by stationarity. Reversing $D$ reverses $k$ and preserves $\eta$, so averaging the right coefficients gives the balanced traces. Each one-sided coefficient is nonnegative at the minimum. When no positive-area supporting trace occurs, the gradient of an integrated hinge is the integral of its smooth parameter gradient against $\mathbf1_{\ell>0}$. The change of this indicator on the same strip has signed derivative $k/\|u\|$ on proper sections and zero on the other sections. The line proof works along any sequence of perturbation directions converging on the unit sphere, with a common strip bound, hence gives a Fréchet derivative of the gradient at zero by compactness. This proves the ordinary Hessian assertion. Finally, restricting to $\gamma=0$ gives $k=D\cdot(w-Y)$ and $\eta=v^{\mathsf T}\Sigma v$, proving the matrix formula.
statement:
Let $\mu$ sum $d$-volume on finitely many compact positive $d$-dimensional convex fibers, $d\ge1$, and fix $Y=(p,y)$, positive definite $\Sigma$, normalized buffer $b\ge0$ and width $h>0$. Let $N=(a,u)$, with $\Gamma(u)=\sqrt{u^{\mathsf T}\Sigma u}=1$, locally minimize the cap integral in all normal parameters through $Y$. For $D=(a',v)$ write
$$
m=N\cdot(w-Y),\qquad q=(m+b)/h,\qquad
\gamma=u^{\mathsf T}\Sigma v,\qquad k=D\cdot(w-Y)-\gamma m,\qquad
\eta=v^{\mathsf T}\Sigma v-\gamma^2,
$$
and set $S=\int\psi(q)d\mu/h,\ A=\int q\psi(q)d\mu$, where $\psi=\Psi'$. Vary the normal by $N+tD$ using
$$
Q(t)=\int\Psi\left(\frac{(N+tD)\cdot(w-Y)/\Gamma(u+tv)+b}{h}\right)d\mu(w).
$$
The first and second derivatives of the normalized margin are $k$ and $-2\gamma k-\eta m$. For a $C^2$ CDF $\Psi$,
$$
Q''(0)=\int\psi'(q)k^2\,d\mu/h^2+(bS-A)\eta\ge0.
$$
The polarized form uses $k_Dk_E$ and $v_D^{\mathsf T}\Sigma v_E-\gamma_D\gamma_E$ in place of $k^2,\eta$. The normalization term vanishes for radial variations $D=N$ and pure-base variations. For an outward kernel with $\psi$ supported on $[-1,0]$, $-hS\le A\le0$.

For the uniform outward ramp $\Psi(q)=(q+1)_+-q_+$, set $c=N\cdot Y-b$. Let $\bar\sigma_\ell$ sum the coarea $d\mathcal H^{d-1}/\|u\|$ on all proper sections at level $N\cdot w=\ell$, with half that coarea on positive-area supporting facets and zero on null or empty sections. Then
$$
\lim_{t\to0}\frac{Q(t)+Q(-t)-2Q(0)}{t^2}
=\frac{\int k^2\,d\bar\sigma_{c-h}-\int k^2\,d\bar\sigma_c}{h}+(bS-A)\eta\ge0.
$$
In the right second derivative $\lim_{t\downarrow0}2(Q(t)-Q(0))/t^2$, replace each half-facet $k^2/2$ by $[k]_-^2$ when the fiber is on the positive side of that endpoint plane, and $[k]_+^2$ when it is on the negative side, retaining the lower plus and upper minus signs. This derivative is also nonnegative. If neither endpoint supports a positive-area facet, the expression is the ordinary Hessian. On the hyperplane $\gamma=0$ the PSD matrix is the lower balanced second-moment matrix of $w-Y$ minus the upper one, plus $h(bS-A)\operatorname{diag}(0,\Sigma)$.
title: Normal Hessian and balanced traces for smoothed minimizing caps
